specLimits.description: The values a reading must stay within to meet the requirement of those it serves, in the KPI's unit: the specification limits a critical-to-quality measure carries (TAXONOMY.md D58). With them, the engine reports the process capability (Cp, Cpk) and sigma level from the readings. Not the control limits, which the engine works out from the readings themselves.

response.description: What is done when a reading signals trouble, so the gain is held (a DMAIC control plan's response plan, TAXONOMY.md D58): what sets it off, what is done, which role does it and how soon.

trigger.description: What sets it off: a reading outside the control or specification limits, a run on one side, a trend.

by.description: The role that acts. Never a person.

withinDays.description: How many days it has to act.

metric.description: How the number is computed from its sources, in the dbt semantic layer's terms (TAXONOMY.md D57), so an analytics engineer can build it as a dbt metric: simple (one measure), ratio (a numerator over a denominator), cumulative (one measure summed over a window) or derived (an expression over other KPIs' metrics).

measure.description: For simple and cumulative: the measure.

denominator.description: For ratio: what it is counted out of.

window.description: For cumulative: how far back it sums, such as 28 days; over all time when left out.

expr.description: For derived: the expression over the metrics it uses, named by their KPIs' ids with hyphens as underscores.

uses.description: For derived: the KPIs whose metrics the expression uses.

filter.description: For an analyst: a dbt where filter on the metric, such as {{ Dimension('depot__region') }} = 'north'. Written from where once its inputs are mapped to dimensions.

where.description: Which rows count, as conditions built from named parts (TAXONOMY.md D63): an input named in the person's words, how it compares and the value. An analyst or an agent writes it as filter later.

input.description: What is compared, named in the person's words, such as the depot's region.

value.description: What it is compared with; for oneOf, the values separated by commas.

name.description: Deprecated: the name is metadata.name, as Kubernetes keeps it. Read from a manifest saved before 2.6.0 and folded into metadata.name; never written.

unit.description: What this is counted in. A reference, not free text, so one quantity is not spelled several ways.

baseline.description: Today's figure and when it was taken, or an admitted unknown with the reason and when it will be known: every measure has one or the other (TAXONOMY.md D25, D26).

sources.description: Every data source the number is read from: one, or several when it is computed from them jointly (a count from one and the total from another), so anyone can go and check each.

source.description: Deprecated: an indicator may be read from several data sources jointly; they are sources. Read from a manifest saved before 2.7.0 and folded into sources; never written.

owner.description: The role that answers for the indicator: keeps its readings coming and says what they mean. A Resource from the catalogue ({"kind":"Resource",...}), a unit of category orgUnit where the unit answers as a whole, or an outside party; never a person. See TAXONOMY.md D44.

goals.description: The aims this indicator measures, at any level: SMART's Measurable is met through a key result or an aligned indicator, at every level (TAXONOMY.md D25).

disaggregations.description: The dimensions this KPI can be broken down by, as Segment references. A reference, not free text: the thing a measure is split by and the thing a gap is observed in are one concept, and free text would give it two names, one of them uncheckable.
